name: Cross-vendor candidate patches selected by executed behaviour, never by model opinion
description: Blueprint 40 of 96 (BP-IMP-03). Several independent vendors each produce a candidate patch; the winner is chosen by EXECUTION on synthesised distinguishing inputs, not by asking a model which patch is best (model-opinion rerank measures about chance on JudgeBench). Candidates are clustered by observed behaviour, crashers and timeouts are knocked out, and the selection signal is agreement between a Claude candidate and a Codex candidate - two SAME-vendor candidates agreeing is not independence and explicitly does not count. When no distinguishing input exists the workflow declares behavioural EQUIVALENCE rather than manufacturing a winner.

task.description: The contested defect or work unit the candidates all address

vendors.description: Independent generators. At least two DIFFERENT vendors - a same-vendor pair cannot supply independence.

test_harness.description: The executable harness. Without it this blueprint is contraindicated - there is nothing to select on.

distinguishing_input_budget.description: Upper bound on synthesised inputs before equivalence is declared

sandbox.description: Executing N unreviewed candidate patches is an execution risk; Windows has no native process sandbox, so `none` is only for read-only candidates

candidate-generator.description: Produces ONE candidate patch with no knowledge of the sibling candidates - contamination would destroy the independence the selection depends on

input-synthesiser.description: Synthesises inputs that reach the lines where the candidates DIVERGE; scores nothing and ranks nothing

executor.description: Runs every candidate on every synthesised input inside the sandbox and records observed behaviour only

aspect-juror.description: Ranks WITHIN the winning behavioural cluster on declared aspects; may never overturn the execution result

routes.reason: the jury must not share a vendor with the candidate it is ranking
execution is mechanical; effort buys nothing and costs quota

stages.title: S0 GENERATE one candidate per vendor, mutually blind

body.title: One vendor, one patch, no sibling context

stages.title: Unreviewed candidate code does not execute on the host
S1 SYNTHESISE inputs that reach the lines where candidates DIVERGE

work_unit.title: Synthesise inputs on which the candidate patches must behave differently, and settle the dispute by executing them
work_unit.question_or_target: Diff the candidate patches, find every line where their behaviour can differ, and synthesise concrete inputs that REACH those lines - including rare branches - up to the declared budget. Emit the inputs plus, for each, which candidates it is predicted to separate. Rank nothing.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: reaching a rare divergent branch is the hardest step in the blueprint; max effort is justified

work_unit.evidence_requirement: for every synthesised input, the executed trace showing the divergent line was actually reached - a predicted-but-unreached input is not a distinguishing input
tests_required: two candidates differing only in a rare branch: the synthesiser must produce an input that reaches it, or report the branch as unreachable within budget
two byte-identical candidates: the synthesiser must return zero inputs and the workflow must declare equivalence, not rank them
both-states control: a seeded subtly-wrong candidate must be separated from a correct one; if the input set separates nothing on a KNOWN difference, the synthesiser is broken
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer who re-executes the input set against the same candidates and reproduces the separation, without reading the synthesiser's rationale
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:TST-0274 emitted only when distinguishing-inputs.json exists, parses, and every listed input carries an execution trace proving the divergent line was reached; otherwise FAILED:TST-0274 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: after two budget exhaustions, enumerate at least two alternative separation strategies (property-based generation, symbolic reach, targeted mutation) before a third attempt

stages.title: S2 EXECUTE every candidate on every synthesised input, inside the sandbox

body.title: Observed behaviour only - exit status, output, timing, crash

stages.title: S3 CLUSTER by observed behaviour; KNOCK OUT crashers and timeouts
The selection signal is EXECUTION; an opinion may not enter here
The agreeing pair must span two vendors - same-vendor agreement is not consensus
S4 RANK within the winning cluster only; the jury cannot overturn execution

impact.blast_radius: candidate patches are executed only inside the declared sandbox and are never applied to the working tree by this workflow

worked_example.scenario: A boundary defect with 3 candidate patches: A (Claude, off-by-one fixed), B (Codex, off-by-one fixed identically in behaviour), C (Claude, fixed the symptom but crashes on an empty input).
worked_example.step_1: vendors=[anthropic, openai, anthropic] -> 3 candidates, mutually blind
worked_example.step_2: the synthesiser diffs them and produces 41 inputs, of which 4 reach the empty-input branch where C differs
worked_example.step_3: execution: A and B agree on all 41; C raises IndexError on the 4 empty-input cases -> knocked out as a crasher
worked_example.step_4: clusters = {A,B} and {C}. The agreeing pair spans anthropic and openai -> independence-gate passes and {A,B} wins
worked_example.counter_case_same_vendor: had the surviving pair been A and C (both anthropic), independence-gate FAILS on agreeing_pair_vendors_distinct == false and no winner is declared on that basis
worked_example.counter_case_equivalence: if A and B are byte-identical, the synthesiser returns 0 inputs and behavioural-equivalence-declared fires with on_stop=emit-partial - the workflow refuses to rank them

x_extensions.distinctive_mechanism: selection by executed behaviour on synthesised divergence inputs, with cross-vendor agreement as the signal and an explicit equivalence verdict instead of a manufactured winner
contraindications: NOT when candidates cannot be executed - with no harness there is no signal and this degenerates into the LLM-judge it exists to replace
NOT for style choices - there is no behaviour to diverge
NOT when one candidate is obviously correct - the machinery costs more than the decision
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-ARC-01 tournaments DESIGNS on a rubric and BP-CNC-06 scores artifacts on weights; this one never scores - it executes, and its jury may only order the survivors of that execution.
